title: Out-of-domain replication — FRANK-XSum (abstractive, hallucination-heavy)
what_this_is: One out-of-domain replication of the judge-validity measurement, on the half of FRANK built from XSum (highly abstractive one-sentence summaries, hallucination-heavy). This is the card that shows WHICH judge survives off-distribution: the NLI judge replicates; the embedding judge collapses to ~zero here.

results.note: REPLICATES the SummEval-level validity out of domain; published parallels on FRANK-XSum: MNLI 0.17, FactCC -0.07.
CI spans zero: the embedding judge is corpus-dependent and collapses on abstractive, hallucination-heavy text. This is why --scorer nli is the load-bearing default.

scope_limits: Human label is Factuality only (narrower than SummEval's 4-axis meaning composite).
One replication corpus is evidence of transfer, not proof of universality.
The committed BillSum golden receipt certifies under the embedding judge; this card is the documented reason new load-bearing work should prefer --scorer nli.
reading_guidance: This is the card a skeptic should read first: it reports the judge family's failure mode (embedding on abstractive text) as prominently as its replication (NLI).
